objective: Resolve Elijah’s early family and distinguish the proved heirship from inferred biological parentage.

questions.question: Was the selected Isaac Elijah’s father?
questions.answer: The original Weakley deed names Elijah Glasgow among the heirs of deceased Isaac Glasgow, conveying land originally surveyed in Isaac’s name. Its numerous coheirs match the existing Isaac family: William C., Wagstaff K., John G., Joseph D. and Jesse Glasgow, with additional initialled Glasgow heirs and the Coffe and Adams couples. This dense family-group match identifies the inherited Elijah–Isaac pair much more securely than birth estimates alone. The already cited 1812 Wake marriage of Isaac Glascoe and Dosha Kanaday removes the former Wake-versus-Currituck objection; the published abstract of Isaac’s 1848 obituary independently reports Currituck origin and migration to Weakley in 1826. Together these support 97% confident fatherhood inference. The deed explicitly establishes heirship, not a literal son clause. Its grantor group includes spouses, so not every grantor is Isaac’s biological child. The confidence concerns Elijah and the existing Isaac family-role identification; no mother, exact vital date, or other child’s father grade is reassessed. The original obituary and marriage bond were not inspected: the obituary is a checked published abstract, and the marriage is a checked index. Other initialled heirs and possible duplicate accounts remain separate questions.

research_state.last_test: Original 1851 deed names Elijah among deceased Isaac’s heirs; matching family supports a confident fatherhood inference.
research_state.next_test: Resolve initialled coheirs and single W.P.M. heir’s possible duplicate accounts; full estate distributions may clarify family capacities.
research_state.reopen_when: A concrete conflicting family or identity record emerges; do not repeat generic census-age matching as an uncompleted father test.
